text: Unbound testosterone is biologically active and available to be taken up by bodily tissues; weakly bound testosterone can rapidly dissociate from albumin and become active (1 19). In its unbound form, testosterone binds to androgen receptors in the cytoplasm of target tissues. This causes a conformational change that shuttles the testosterone-androgen receptor complex to the nucleus of the cell, where it regulates gene transcription (240).
